title: Quant Stability Playbook — scratchpad
content:
Goal: capture a lightweight playbook for diagnosing and mitigating stability regressions when we push low-bit (4/3/2-bit) model variants into the serving stack. This is a personal scratchpad — messy, pragmatic, and intentionally shallow in places.

Why I care (quick):
- Dedicated customers want 2–4x cost reduction; quant seems the main lever.
- We keep seeing occasional token-level divergences and rare hangs after KV-cache eviction. Need reproducible triage steps.

What I read this sprint (short notes + what stuck):
1) "Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models" (unofficial repo link) — good survey of per-channel vs per-tensor scaling. Note: per-channel seems to preserve attention heads better but complicates kernel code.
2) "Quantization-aware KV cache maintenance" (workshop paper) — suggests adjusting cache storage format to keep per-key scale metadata; appears to reduce catastrophic attention dropout on long contexts.
3) Engineer blog: "When low-bit meets beam instability" — practical troubleshooting steps (re-run with FP16 on same seeds, check topk temperature shifts).

Key takeaways:
- Many instabilities are input-distribution dependent; we only surface them on specific long-prompt shapes or rapid prefix-length jumps.
- Cache eviction logic + quant rounding interact badly: re-quantizing cached tensors can introduce sub-token jumps if scale mismatches.
- Deterministic seeding helps reproduce some failures but not all — nondeterminism often hides in fused CUDA kernels.

Immediate experiments to run (priority order):
- Exp A: Reproduce failing transcript from customer X with quant-4 and full FP16 on same infra (dedicated node). Metrics: token divergence rate at 1k/2k/4k, throughput, GPU memory. Expected: divergence appears after the first eviction.
- Exp B: Add per-key scale metadata to KV cache serialization; re-run same transcript. Compare L2 difference and divergence onset.
- Exp C: Offline fuzz tester: random prefix lengths + random stop tokens to stress eviction paths for 12h across model variants. Log full seeds and kernel versions.

Minimal instrumentation to add (dev tasks):
- Save raw cached KV tensors (pre- and post-eviction) for failing sessions (s3 bucket: s3://redwood-qa/quant-playbook/noelle).
- Add a lightweight histogram of quant scales per-layer per-head to runtime metrics (console: per-request optional tag).
- Expose an "eviction-compare" debug route that returns L2/linf diffs between fallback FP16 outputs and quant variant for the last N tokens.

Hypotheses & checks: 
H1: Scale drift across batched requests causes mismatched dequantization when merging KV caches. Check: compare per-key scales before merge.
H2: Kernel non-determinism in int ops introduces rare token flips at low probability. Check: run with CUDA deterministic flags and narrow kernel choices.
H3: Temperature/topk interplay magnifies small numeric differences into different decoding branches. Check: run greedy vs sampling and compare branching points.

Quick checklist for triage when a customer reports a quant regression: 
- Get exact model variant + quant config + runtime binary hash + kernel list.
- Pull full transcript + seed + request metadata + route config (batching, prefetch).
- Re-run locally with: (1) FP16; (2) quant variant w/ per-request debug logging; (3) quant variant with disabled cache to isolate cache.
- Upload cached KV dumps to s3 and run diff tool (script: tools/kv-quant-diff.py).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Storage cost vs benefit for per-key scales in cache: how big are the metadata overheads at 512–1k token contexts? rough calc needed.
- Are there model architectures (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder hybrids) where per-channel quant has more fragility in attention? Need to catalog across our model zoo.
- Can we craft a micro-fuzz corpus that reliably triggers the brittle cases? Current random fuzzers give low signal-to-noise.

Notes to self (practical):
- Talk to kai about instrumenting the dedicated staging cluster with extra debug buckets — avoid hitting prod logging rate limits.
- Ping zara for her KV cache proto sketches (she said she'd share in #kv-cache thread).
- Sketch for a small PR: add flag --save-kv-debug to runtime so failing requests can be triaged without full repro. Target: tiny API surface change + telemetry opt-in.

Draft experiment schedule (2-week sprint format):
Week 1: repro attempts (Exp A), collect KV dumps, baseline histograms.
Week 2: implement per-key scale serialization + run Exp B; run 48h fuzzing (Exp C) in parallel.

Outputs I want by end of sprint:
- reproducible minimal example (transcript + runbook) that triggers divergence at least 3x out of 5 runs 
- a short playbook note (1–2 page) summarizing triage steps, to land in Confluence (link: CONFLUENCE-QUANT-PLAYBOOK-2026).
- a small runtime PR that enables kv-dump and a debug metric histogram.

References & quick links (copied while reading):
- https://example.org/papers/post-training-quant-survey.pdf
- https://engineer-blog.redwood/internal/when-lowbit-meets-beam 
- github: pull/874 (runtime changes discussion)

Random heuristics I've been jotting down:
- If divergence begins right after eviction and the L2 between pre/post cached tensors > 1e-3 relative, treat as high-priority.
- If re-running with CUDA deterministic flags removes divergence, file kernel-level investigation (tag: sre-kernel).

TODO (short):
- [ ] Kick off Exp A on staging, save logs to s3 (owner: noelle)
- [ ] Short sync with kai (15m) to review instrument plan
- [ ] Draft PR stub for --save-kv-debug (owner: noelle)
summary: Personal scratchpad capturing reading notes, concrete experiments, triage checklist, and a two-week plan to investigate quantization stability issues in serving.
